candidate: Proposed C-origin: direct PM/Y origin contexts + real headless TS authority + local SQLite; packaged host still unqualified
preconditions: Read architecture-review.md, F006/F007 and existing table/product/API contracts.
Freeze exact versioned Y payload envelope, accepted/provisional/committed state transition, context/operation identity and SQL transaction schema before implementation.
Keep prior matched contract unchanged and all raw controls; no dependency upgrades without separate manifest/evidence.
Real process owns state and SQL; Playwright may drive UI but cannot implement an owner or a second reducer.
G-J is cases01–10; G-N case11 and required host/security gates; G-M cases12–13. These do not replace full feature/release tests.
scope_boundaries: No production implementation authorized by this contract.
No live provider/cloud collaboration, full entity/scheduler feature coverage, GC/migration/export or cross-Space feature promise.
Engine binary encoding is an experimental candidate, not accepted production native format.
No restart serialization promise for selective undo stacks; retained document history/pins remain required.
SIGKILL proves only the executed process-failure profile; native flush and OS/power failure require separate evidence.

cases.title: Canonical codec survives owner restart
cases.action: Serialize one versioned accepted Y-state root into SQLite. Kill owner; reopen without any PM JSON/body cache.
cases.expected: Both real editor views reconstruct equal validated PM content and stable Clutter IDs from committed bytes; no independent JSON/Markdown fallback.

cases.title: Commit before accepted publication
cases.action: With two real EditorViews connected to a real owner, inject precommit failure during an edit.
cases.expected: Accepted engine/root/revision/receipt stay old together; provisional input and history remain available/protected. No post-hoc rollback of a published accepted Y mutation.

cases.title: Unknown commit and lost editor reply
cases.action: Pause/kill at before commit, after commit and before reply, including a real full-editor operation. Retry after reconnect using same operation ID.
cases.expected: Before commit: no effect/receipt. After commit: exact original durable root/receipt; one effect. Resolve unknown COMMIT before further writes/publishing a conflicting live root; preserve unaccepted input.

cases.title: Two real editor views plus CLI and MCP
cases.action: Alternate overlapping/disjoint changes from A/B and real subprocess CLI/MCP through the same owner.
cases.expected: Accepted state converges, each input applied once, no lost foreign text, native selections remain view-local; no Playwright-owned authority or read-only projection stand-in.

cases.title: Context undo through durable command path
cases.action: Repeat unchanged applicable matched-history assertions while CLI/MCP insert foreign work; destroy and remount both actual editor views.
cases.expected: Context history survives view destruction, safe inverses still apply and foreign work remains. Protective refusals are distinct from applied undo. Every accepted inverse/redo has coherent committed outcome.

cases.title: Protection and failed-close integration
cases.action: Pause acceptance, type in A, close its view with failed main save; inject protection failure and success separately.
cases.expected: Failed protection keeps work/session alive and blocks destructive close. Successful protection commits full pending closure/base/generation before allowing close; not a flag-only UI save.

cases.title: Owner restart with pending work
cases.action: Commit newer protected generation, attempt stale cleanup, kill owner, reconnect both clients and inspect recovery.
cases.expected: No stale resurrection/deletion; accepted content and pending draft remain distinct. Explicit same-base recovery applies once; newer-current conflict preserves draft. Restart interactive-history boundary is declared, not fake restored UndoManager state.

cases.title: Missed events and transport echoes
cases.action: Suppress notifications, suspend one client, accept a command and its retry, then resume and resync by revision.
cases.expected: Both editor replicas catch up from durable revision truth; no echoed duplicate or silent cursor reset. Unprotected input is not discarded merely because the replica missed a hint.

cases.title: Editor payload admission and schema bounds
cases.action: Send malformed/oversized update, forged context/origin, invalid task ID/shape or read-only embed mutation; then a valid edit.
cases.expected: Reject unsafe admission without accepted root/outcome mutation or input loss; valid later edit still works. Internal Y origin is not a client grant; no direct raw-update bypass in public CLI/MCP.

cases.title: Same identity and real process contention
cases.action: Race exact duplicate commands from editor/CLI/MCP, changed-ID reuse, two owners and a paused incumbent; rotate credentials after a real restart.
cases.expected: One semantic effect/original receipt; changed reuse/wrong destination/old capabilities denied. Paused owner retains exclusion; no independent writer fallback or token-as-operation identity.

cases.title: Targeted native and installed headless smoke
cases.action: On exact signed/packaged Mac candidate, launch CLI with desktop closed, attach two native editor views, undo/redo through view remount, exercise confirmed table modes, failed close and owner restart.
cases.expected: Record actual runtime/SQLite/OS/filesystem/input route and outcomes. CLI/MCP work without developer Node or a window; shell exit does not kill protected in-flight owner. Only new integration risks retested; earlier manual results stay valid. IME unavailable/VoiceOver deferred remain labelled, never inferred pass.

cases.title: Atomic task identity and historical restore closure
cases.action: Using proposed production entity representation, move one task with body/properties from note1 to note2, crash around commit and restore a historical note after that task moved.
cases.expected: Exactly one active placement and one canonical body/properties; old-or-new move closure and one outcome. Historical note stays historical; restore rechecks placement and refuses conflicts rather than duplicating or relocating silently. Not the one-document embedded-task fixture.

cases.title: External asset commit and retained root closure
cases.action: Stage valid pinned PNG/PDF fixtures as external immutable files, fault before/after publication and SQL reference commit, then retain/pin/read an old root after removing current reference.
cases.expected: No acknowledged root references absent/partial bytes; atomic or replay-safe publication with verified hashes/flush profile. Old pinned versions keep required assets. Orphans do not become current or get unsafe cleanup. This is not in-DB BLOB coverage or full media render acceptance.

codec_envelope_proposal.payload: One Y.encodeStateAsUpdate accepted-state binary payload using pinned Yjs13.6.33 initially. Full state per retained fixture revision; validate decoded PM through the pinned schema. No second authoritative PM JSON/Markdown body.
codec_envelope_proposal.metadata: Space/document/version/parent and semantic/engine decoder versions are SQL root metadata committed with payload bytes/hash and original outcome. State vector is derived, not a content hash or authoritative revision.
codec_envelope_proposal.scope: One synthetic document, existing semantic fixture only. Production entity/property layout and multi-document closure are G-M; no external format acceptance.
codec_envelope_proposal.unsupported: Unknown format/schema/engine codec refuses writable open without overwriting existing roots; no silent decode fallback or migration.

acceptance_state_machine_proposal.rule: Authenticate destination/grant/context. Stable semantic request fingerprint includes operationId, space/document and operation arguments; transport bearer/owner generation are excluded from semantic identity. Resolve exact prior outcome before expectedVersion checks. Reject changed reuse.

Starting from authoritative committed version, apply bounded proposed operation/update only to isolated staging state; validate full semantic/asset closure and map required selection/context effects. Preserve original provisional peer input; never mutate accepted live state before SQL.

Serialized owner commits new Y root/parent/version and original outcome together. Retain all fixture roots/receipts; no GC, migrations or independent body writes. A changed accepted root increments content version once; no-change/metadata receipt cannot fabricate a content edit.

On uncertain COMMIT result, stop further mutation admission until query/reopen resolves durable root/outcome. Do not publish staged state or reject as definitely unexecuted. Reconnect and retry same semantic ID; if root cannot be resolved, fail closed preserving provisional input.

After known committed state, reconcile accepted in-memory engine from committed bytes/operation and publish revision-tagged updates. Failure between COMMIT and publication is catch-up work, never transaction rollback. Notifications are hints; readers fetch authoritative revision.

A precommit failure leaves accepted state old. Provisional edit/context history stays recoverable or is durably protected with base/generation before destructive close. On owner restart separate protected input from accepted state and use declared interactive-history boundary; no automatic stale overwrite.
